[b][size=xx-large][color=#ffffff][u]Hack Forum News - Edition 37[/u][/color][/size][/b]

[b]Welcome back to the Hack Forum News. Where we keep you up to date on the weekly events and news happening on site and around the world. If you have never heard of the Hack Forum News, don't worry, we have you covered. We are a team of members from the Hack Forums community who are journalists and writers, and we are here to keep you in the loop of the changes around the site and the events happening around the world.[/b]

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6319690][color=#ffffff]Server Move[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

[mention=1] has been working hard again this week with the whole new server. We have mentioned this thread again as it's the main area getting worked on right now. We know it is taking its time, but the hard part is currently being worked on and from what we have seen so far, everything is going quite well. If you haven't been keeping up to date with what is happening, check this thread out as it will allow you to understand the full details & give you all a little better of a scope about what is going on at the back end of the work and why it is taking a while for this to be fully completed.

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6314337][color=#ffffff]The Hack Forums Wiki Returns[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=2331053]

The Hack Forums Wiki has returned. The site has been under some work recently as the site was sadly left with a load of issues and no one was running the official site. Thanks to everyone within the HF news team, the site is now under new leadership and, thanks to [mention=1] allowing the team to start their work on this while maintaining the HF news, the site is back getting some lovely changes and getting updated daily to bring it back to a new modern day Wikipedia with a load of information for everyone to read up on.

[size=xx-large][color=#00D9FF]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6320254]Every AI chat assistant is now an ad company?[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=4931690] [/b][/color][/size]

A thread that cuts straight into the uncomfortable future: if an assistant can shape what you read, buy, and believe, it becomes one of the most valuable "ad surfaces" ever created. Replies lean into the inevitability of data-driven influence, the classic "if it's free, you're the product" line, and the privacy spiral of people oversharing with AI like it's therapy. [i]It's the kind of discussion that makes you re-check your own boundaries with these tools.[/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#00FF88]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6320890]If WW3 started tomorrow what would actually pump?[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=4595369] [/b][/color][/size]

A blunt "markets under stress" question that instantly turned into a mix of dark humor and practical takes. People throw out everything from raw materials tied to war production, to defense names, to the usual "essentials" list (batteries, dry food). It's chaotic in the most HF way - part macro chat, part edgy one-liners - but it does surface the obvious truth: conflict reshuffles demand fast, and sentiment moves money even faster. [i]Not financial advice, just a very real snapshot of how people think under "what if" pressure.[/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#FF6B00]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6320904]Hey everyone! How did you find hackforums?[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=2207123] [/b][/color][/size]

A wholesome lounge prompt that turned into a mini oral history of HF. You get the full spectrum: friends inviting friends, people searching "hacking forums" back in the day, and the classic pipeline of "came for game hacks / drama / curiosity, stayed for IT, infosec, and community." [i]One of those threads that quietly reminds you why forums still matter.[/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#FF00FF]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6320865]Small Things That Can Actually Make You Happy, But Most People Dont Notice[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=2207123] [/b][/color][/size]

Simple prompt, surprisingly warm responses. Little wins like nostalgia hits, tiny surprises, affectionate moments, and even random animals approaching on night walks - it's the "human" side of HF that doesn't show up in the usual tech/cyber threads. [i]Good palate cleanser if your feed's been doom-heavy lately.[/i]

[hr]

[size=xx-large][color=#FFD700]▸[/color][/size] [u][b][size=x-large][color=#ffffff][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6320617]So....Basically....[/url][/color][/size][/b][/u]
[size=small][color=#888888][b]by [mention=1] [/b][/color][/size]

This one's a fun meta-spiral: language quirks ("so", "basically", "irregardless", starting with "I") as a window into how people think, speak, and self-edit - with AI as the mirror. The thread bounces between "AI can help you self-reflect" and the pushback that LLMs don't truly "learn you," while others share how they've adapted their wording just to avoid being judged for filler phrases. [i]It's part linguistics, part psychology, part modern internet insecurity - and weirdly relatable.[/i]

[hr]

[img]https://hackforums.net/images/hfnews/ves-brown.png[/img]
[size=medium][b]Writer -[/b][/size] [mention=5458992]

[color=#C10300][b][size=15]Silent Heart Risk in Your 30s[/size][/b][/color]

Many men in their 30s feel healthy but may already have early artery changes. High stress, smoking, poor diet, and lack of exercise quietly increase blood pressure and cholesterol. These risk factors often show no symptoms until serious damage occurs. A simple blood test, blood pressure check, and regular physical activity can significantly reduce long-term heart disease risk. Prevention in your 30s is an investment in your 50s.
[hr]

[color=#00369B][size=15]Advice of the week[/size][/color]

Stop waiting to feel “ready.”
Most growth begins in discomfort, not confidence. If you wait until you feel fully prepared, you’ll wait forever.
Start before you feel ready. Learn while doing. Adjust as you go.
Progress creates confidence — not the other way around.
[hr]

[color=#008E02][size=15]
Quote of the week[/size] [/color]
“Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most.”
— Abraham Lincoln
